title: Etale cohomology continuity for a uniformly bounded-below system of complexes
statement: Let $X=\varprojlim_{i\in I}X_i$ be a cofiltered inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition maps $f_{i'i}:X_{i'}\to X_i$, and let $f_i:X\to X_i$ be the projections. For each $i$, let $\mathcal F_i^\bullet$ be a complex of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] on $X_i$, with morphisms of complexes $\varphi_{i'i}:f_{i'i}^{-1}\mathcal F_i^\bullet\to\mathcal F_{i'}^\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] for $i'\geq i$, compatible in the sense that $\varphi_{i''i}=\varphi_{i''i'}\circ f_{i''i'}^{-1}\varphi_{i'i}$ whenever $i''\geq i'\geq i$ (using the canonical identification $f_{i''i'}^{-1}f_{i'i}^{-1}\cong f_{i''i}^{-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]). Suppose one integer $a$ satisfies $\mathcal F_i^n=0$ for every $i$ and every $n<a$. Set $\mathcal F^\bullet=\varinjlim_i f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i^\bullet$, the colimit taken termwise. Then the canonical pullback maps induce, for every integer $p$, an isomorphism $\varinjlim_i H^p((X_i)_{\Et},\mathcal F_i^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^p(X_{\Et},\mathcal F^\bullet)$, with complex cohomology defined by derived global sections [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text: Put $\mathcal F^\bullet=\varinjlim_i f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i^\bullet$ termwise. For every pair of integers $(p,n)$, apply the sheaf continuity theorem [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-limit-of-schemes] to the system of sheaves $\mathcal F_i^n$ and its compatible transition maps. Its hypotheses are exactly the quasi-compact quasi-separated stages, affine transitions, and the colimit sheaf $\mathcal F^n$, so it gives a canonical isomorphism $\varinjlim_i H^p((X_i)_{\Et},\mathcal F_i^n)\cong H^p(X_{\Et},\mathcal F^n)$.

proof.text: Use [thm-sp-if-e1] with the global-sections functor, as identified for etale sheaves by [def-sp-etale-dictionary] and for complexes by [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. Its indexing is $E_{1,i}^{p,q}=H^p((X_i)_{\Et},\mathcal F_i^q)$ and $E_1^{p,q}=H^p(X_{\Et},\mathcal F^q)$: $p$ is the cohomological degree and $q$ is the filtration degree. The comparison [lem-weil-pbc-complex-spectral-sequence-comparison] has four hypotheses. (i) Step 1 gives $\varinjlim_i E_{1,i}^{p,q}\cong E_1^{p,q}$ for every $p,q$, and [lem-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-e1-pullback-functorial] identifies this with the map of $E_1$ pages. (ii) Each row resolution starts in cohomological degree $p=0$, while $\mathcal F_i^q=\mathcal F^q=0$ for $q<a$, so all $E_1$ terms vanish for $p<0$ or $q<a$. (iii) In total degree $n$, only $a\leq q\leq n$ and $p=n-q\geq0$ occur, uniformly in $i$; these bounds force stabilization of each page entry. (iv) The filtration by the second degree in [thm-sp-if-e1] and its finite-filtration convergence [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] give $F^qA_i^n=A_i^n$ and $F^qA^n=A^n$ for $q\leq a$, zero for $q>n$, and $E_\infty^{p,q}=\operatorname{gr}^q A^{p+q}$ (similarly at each stage). The functoriality node supplies the compatible spectral-sequence maps, filtered abutment maps, and graded compatibility. Thus the comparison node gives $\varinjlim_i A_i^n\cong A^n$.

proof.text: By [def-sp-kinjective-bridge] and [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], the abutments $A_i^n$ and $A^n$ of Step 2 are $H^n((X_i)_{\Et},\mathcal F_i^\bullet)$ and $H^n(X_{\Et},\mathcal F^\bullet)$ defined by derived global sections. For a transition $f_{i'i}$ use the pair $(f_{i'i},\varphi_{i'i})$ in [lem-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-e1-pullback-functorial]; for the map to $X$ use $(f_i,\iota_i)$, where $\iota_i:f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i^\bullet\to\mathcal F^\bullet$ is the colimit coprojection. The identity and composition clauses of that node, together with the cocycle condition in the statement, show that these give the compatible transition and target maps required in Step 2. Its abutment clause identifies each $b_i^n$ with the canonical derived pullback map, so the isomorphism from Step 2 is exactly the displayed one.
